speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers have the prerogative to decide how to structure workers’ overall compensation, provided they comply with PWM requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: PWM requirements increase year on year and there is a limit to how much wage components can be shifted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This means that security officers will likely see that total take-home pay, which includes both basic wages and variable components, such as allowances, increase over the coming years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Security officers who wish to report contractual breaches or employers not adhering to PWM requirements can approach their union or contact the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) for assistance.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And related to that, how is MOM ensuring that security officers are not subjected to arbitrarily low overtime pay, now that they rely on employer-determined overtime rates?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Lastly, will the Ministry consider increasing the salary threshold for Part 4 protections so that security officers can retain essential protections under the Act, even as wages rise?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In fact, it is a good thing actually that our security officers now earn above what is covered in the Employment Act, Part 4, because, ultimately, this means that their wages now are growing beyond the bottom 20% mark.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Technically, if you want to go by strict definitions, they are exceeding past what we used to think as low-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, that is good progress from the unions and the tripartite partners in terms of how we have managed to increase the low wages of security officers such that by 2028, they will even get up to $3,500, which is much higher than what many of our low-wage workers earn today.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, to a large extent, that shows progress.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I just want to assure the Member that security officers are not worse off in terms of the maximum number of overtime hours or paid leave entitlements because, ultimately, security officers continue to be licensed by the Singapore Police Force's (SPF's) Police Licensing and Regulatory Department.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, the relevant provisions of the Employment Act still apply to them.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, this ensures that there is no gaming, hopefully.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But if there was any gaming, please surface it to us and we will take them to task with the Police.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are aspects in which there is still protection available because this is a licensed sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Nonetheless, having said that, one of the key reasons why we moved towards a gross wage structure for PWM is to make sure that they do not game the system, such that everything is all-in or all-encompassing, and as long as you meet the PWM requirements for gross wage, I think that is sufficient to ensure that there is a minimum amount that security officers can benefit from PWM.
